done_when: each forge work round and each forge close appends one JSON line per step (worker round, review, CI wait) to .git/forge/timings.jsonl, never committed, with the item, the step, the model and effort where one ran, start time, seconds taken and outcome; a failed write never fails the command; a test through the real commands proves the lines

findings.body: Both new tests use the Claude-only fixture (`tests/test_close.py:229`). No test reads timings.jsonl after a Codex worker round, although that path has separate completion handling and switches subsequent rounds to the Fix model (`src/forge/worker.py:62–64`). Omitting timing records for Codex, or recording the wrong outcome or model on subsequent rounds, would pass the suite's timing assertions. Add command-level coverage using the existing Codex service stub for initial and subsequent rounds, including an unsuccessful turn.
findings.title: Not done: prove Codex worker-round timings through forge work

findings.body: The timing assertions exercise only a clean review and passing CI; the sole unsuccessful timing case is a Claude worker failure. Existing close failure tests (`tests/test_close.py:411–438`) do not inspect timings.jsonl. Consequently, dropping review or CI timing records on exceptions, or always reporting successful outcomes, would escape these tests. Extend the real-command tests to assert appended records and outcomes for a blocked review, an unsuccessful review, and failed CI checks.
findings.title: Not done: prove timing records for blocked and failed close steps

why: Forge records no timings, so nobody can tell how long worker rounds, reviews and CI waits take or which models and steps are worth tuning
